metadata.title: Online Learning for Matrix Factorization and Sparse Coding
metadata.authors: Julien Mairal, Francis Bach, Jean Ponce, Guillermo Sapiro

nodes.name: Empirical cost $f_n(\D)$
nodes.statement: $f_n(\D) \defin \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \l(\x_i,\D)$, where $\D \in \Real^{m \times k}$ is the dictionary and $\l$ is a loss function.
nodes.statement_clean: Average loss of the dictionary on a finite training set.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ sparse coding loss $\l(\x,\D)$
nodes.statement: $\l(\x,\D) \defin \min_{\alphab \in \Real^k} \frac{1}{2}\|\x-\D\alphab\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\alphab\|_1$ (basis pursuit / Lasso).
nodes.statement_clean: Optimal value of the $\ell_1$-regularized least-squares decomposition of $\x$ over $\D$.

nodes.name: Constraint set $\C$ for the dictionary
nodes.statement: $\C \defin \{ \D \in \Real^{m \times k} \st \forall j,~\d_j^T\d_j \leq 1 \}$, the set of dictionaries with unit-norm columns.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex set of dictionaries whose columns lie in the unit $\ell_2$-ball.

nodes.name: Expected cost $f(\D)$
nodes.statement: $f(\D) \defin \E_{\x}[\l(\x,\D)] = \lim_{n\to\infty} f_n(\D)$ a.s., the expectation of the loss under the data distribution $p(\x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Population-level loss of a dictionary $\D$.

nodes.name: Quadratic surrogate $\hatf_t(\D)$
nodes.statement: $\hatf_t(\D) \defin \frac{1}{t}\sum_{i=1}^t \big(\frac{1}{2}\|\x_i-\D\alphab_i\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\alphab_i\|_1\big)$, a quadratic-in-$\D$ aggregate of past sparse codes that upper-bounds the empirical cost.
nodes.statement_clean: Aggregate quadratic surrogate of the empirical cost using past coefficients.

nodes.name: Sufficient statistics $\A_t,\B_t$
nodes.statement: $\A_t = \sum_{i=1}^t \alphab_i\alphab_i^T \in \Real^{k\times k}$ and $\B_t = \sum_{i=1}^t \x_i\alphab_i^T \in \Real^{m\times k}$ summarize all past coefficients without storing them individually.
nodes.statement_clean: Two cumulative matrices that fully determine the surrogate $\hatf_t$.

nodes.name: Elastic-net constraint set
nodes.statement: $\C' \defin \{ \D \st \forall j,~ \|\d_j\|_2^2 + \gamma\|\d_j\|_1 \leq 1 \}$, mixing $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ constraints to enforce sparsity in dictionary columns.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex set imposing combined $\ell_1 + \ell_2$ constraints on each dictionary column.

nodes.name: Fused-lasso operator $\FL(\u)$
nodes.statement: For $\u \in \Real^m$, $\FL(\u) \defin \sum_{i=2}^m |\u[i]-\u[i-1]|$, the $\ell_1$ norm of consecutive differences.
nodes.statement_clean: Total variation penalty promoting piecewise-constant vectors.

nodes.name: $\ell_{1,2}$ joint-sparsity norm
nodes.statement: $\|\alphab\|_{1,2} \defin \sum_{j=1}^k \|\alphab^j\|_2$, the $\ell_1$-norm of the $\ell_2$-norms of the rows of $\alphab$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex relaxation of joint row-sparsity used for group / simultaneous sparse coding.

nodes.name: Dictionary learning (joint matrix factorization)
nodes.statement: $\min_{\D \in \C,\alphab \in \Real^{k \times n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(\frac{1}{2}\|\x_i-\D\alphab_i\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\alphab_i\|_1\big)$, equivalently a sparsity-penalized matrix factorization.
nodes.statement_clean: Jointly learn a unit-norm dictionary $\D$ and sparse codes $\alphab$ minimizing reconstruction plus $\ell_1$ penalty.

nodes.name: Expected-cost dictionary learning
nodes.statement: $\min_{\D \in \C} f(\D) = \E_{\x}[\l(\x,\D)]$, the population-level dictionary learning problem.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the expected $\ell_1$ sparse-coding loss over the constraint set $\C$.

nodes.name: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF)
nodes.statement: $\min_{\D, \alphab} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{2}\|\x_i-\D\alphab_i\|_2^2 \st \D \geq 0,~\alphab_i \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Factor a data matrix into a product of two non-negative matrices.

nodes.name: Non-negative sparse coding (NNSC)
nodes.statement: $\min_{\D, \alphab} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(\frac{1}{2}\|\x_i-\D\alphab_i\|_2^2 + \lambda \sum_j \alphab_i[j]\big) \st \D \geq 0,~\alphab_i \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: NMF with an additional sparsity penalty on the codes.

nodes.name: Sparse PCA via dictionary learning
nodes.statement: $\min_{\alphab} \sum_{i=1}^n \big(\frac{1}{2}\|\x_i-\D\alphab_i\|_2^2 + \lambda\|\alphab_i\|_1\big) \st \forall j,~\|\d_j\|_2^2 + \gamma\|\d_j\|_1 \leq 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: SPCA recast as sparse matrix factorization with elastic-net constraint on $\D$.

nodes.name: Constrained sparse coding loss $\l'$
nodes.statement: $\l'(\x,\D) = \min_{\alphab} \|\x-\D\alphab\|_2^2 \st \|\alphab\|_1 \leq T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lasso-style sparse coding with a hard $\ell_1$ constraint.

nodes.name: Constrained sparse coding loss $\l''$
nodes.statement: $\l''(\x,\D) = \min_{\alphab} \|\alphab\|_1 \st \|\x-\D\alphab\|_2^2 \leq \varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sparse coding with a hard reconstruction-error constraint.

nodes.name: Elastic-net projection problem
nodes.statement_clean: Euclidean projection onto the elastic-net constraint ball.

nodes.name: Fused-lasso signal approximation $\P(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)$
nodes.statement: $\min_{\u \in \Real^m} \frac{1}{2}\|\b-\u\|_2^2 + \gamma_1\|\u\|_1 + \gamma_2 \FL(\u) + \frac{\gamma_3}{2}\|\u\|_2^2$, extending Friedman et al.'s fused-lasso signal approximator with an extra Tikhonov term.
nodes.statement_clean: Fused-lasso signal approximation with $\ell_1$, total-variation, and ridge penalties.

nodes.name: (A) Compactly supported data
nodes.statement: The data distribution $p(\x)$ has compact support $K$.
nodes.statement_clean: Data lies in a bounded set $K$, natural for image / audio applications.

nodes.name: (B) Strictly convex surrogates with lower-bounded Hessians
nodes.statement: The smallest eigenvalue of $\frac{1}{t}\A_t$ is $\geq \kappa_1 > 0$ for all $t$, so $\hatf_t$ is strictly convex with Hessian $\I \otimes \frac{2}{t}\A_t$.
nodes.statement_clean: Past-coefficient covariance is uniformly invertible, giving strictly convex surrogates.

nodes.name: (C) Uniqueness condition for sparse coding
nodes.statement: There exists $\kappa_2 > 0$ such that for all $\x \in K$ and all $\D$ visited, the smallest eigenvalue of $\D_\Lambda^T \D_\Lambda$ is $\geq \kappa_2$, where $\Lambda$ is the active set at the solution.
nodes.statement_clean: Active-set Gram matrices are uniformly invertible, ensuring a unique Lasso solution.

nodes.name: Online Dictionary Learning
nodes.statement: Online stochastic-approximation algorithm that alternates LARS-based sparse coding with a quadratic-surrogate dictionary update parameterized by sufficient statistics $\A_t,\B_t$.

nodes.name: Dictionary Update (block-coordinate descent)
nodes.statement: Block-coordinate descent that sequentially updates each column $\d_j$ of $\D$ via $\u_j \leftarrow \frac{1}{\A[j,j]}(\b_j-\D\a_j)+\d_j$ then projects onto the unit $\ell_2$-ball.
output: Updated dictionary $\D$ minimizing the surrogate $\hatf_t$ over $\C$

nodes.name: Mini-batch extension
nodes.statement: Replace single-sample updates by averaging over $\eta$ signals per iteration: $\A_t \leftarrow \A_{t-1}+\frac{1}{\eta}\sum_i \alphab_{t,i}\alphab_{t,i}^T$, $\B_t \leftarrow \B_{t-1}+\frac{1}{\eta}\sum_i \x_{t,i}\alphab_{t,i}^T$.

nodes.name: Past-data scaling with parameter $\rho$
nodes.statement: Replace updates of $\A_t,\B_t$ by $\A_t \leftarrow \beta_t \A_{t-1}+\alphab_t\alphab_t^T$ and $\B_t \leftarrow \beta_t \B_{t-1}+\x_t \alphab_t^T$ with $\beta_t = (1-1/t)^\rho$, geometrically downweighting older statistics.

nodes.name: Linear-time projection on the elastic-net constraint
nodes.statement: Randomized partition-based scheme that identifies the active set $S(\lambda^\star)$ of the projection in expected $\O(m)$ time, then computes $\lambda^\star$ in closed form and applies elastic-net soft thresholding.

nodes.name: Homotopy method for fused-lasso signal approximation
nodes.statement: LARS-style homotopy on the fused-lasso path $\P(\tau\gamma_1,\tau\gamma_2,\tau\gamma_3)$ that exploits the bidiagonal structure of the difference operator to achieve $O(ms)$ time.

nodes.name: LARS-Lasso (homotopy method)
nodes.statement: Cholesky-based homotopy algorithm that returns the entire $\ell_1$-regularization path of the Lasso; used as the sparse coding subroutine.
nodes.origin_citation: Osborne et al. 2000; Efron et al. 2004

nodes.name: First-order projected stochastic gradient descent (baseline)
nodes.statement: Update $\D_t = \Pi_\C[\D_{t-1} - \delta_t \nabla_{\D}\l(\x_t,\D_{t-1})]$ with learning rate $\delta_t = a/(t+b)$; baseline for empirical comparison.

nodes.name: Dictionary update minimization
nodes.statement: $\D_t = \arg\min_{\D \in \C} \frac{1}{t}\big(\frac{1}{2}\trace(\D^T\D\A_t) - \trace(\D^T\B_t)\big)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form quadratic surrogate the dictionary update minimizes.

nodes.name: Per-column update rule
nodes.statement: $\u_j \leftarrow \frac{1}{\A[j,j]}(\b_j-\D\a_j)+\d_j$; $\d_j \leftarrow \frac{1}{\max(\|\u_j\|_2,1)}\u_j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Block-coordinate update for the $j$-th dictionary column with projection onto the unit ball.

nodes.name: Lasso optimality conditions
nodes.statement: $\d_j^T(\x-\D\alphab) = \lambda \sign(\alphab[j])$ if $\alphab[j] \neq 0$, else $|\d_j^T(\x-\D\alphab)| \leq \lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: KKT conditions for the $\ell_1$-regularized least-squares problem.

nodes.name: Closed-form active-set Lasso solution
nodes.statement: $\alphab^\star_\Lambda = (\D_\Lambda^T\D_\Lambda)^{-1}(\D_\Lambda^T\x - \lambda \epsilonb_\Lambda)$ when $\D_\Lambda^T\D_\Lambda$ is invertible.
nodes.statement_clean: Restricted-to-active-set explicit solution for the Lasso.

nodes.name: Kalman-style recursion
nodes.statement: $\D_t \leftarrow \D_{t-1} + (\x_t-\D_{t-1}\alphab_t)\alphab_t^T \big(\sum_{i=1}^t \alphab_i\alphab_i^T\big)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Second-order stochastic-gradient / Kalman recursion arising in the simplified setting where $\alphab_t$ is independent of $\D$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic variations of $\D_t$
nodes.statement: Under (A)-(C), $\D_{t+1}-\D_t = \O(1/t)$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_clean: Successive iterates of the algorithm differ by $O(1/t)$, ensuring summability of squared increments.
assumptions: (B) lower bound $\kappa_1$ on the smallest eigenvalue of $\frac{1}{t}\A_t$

nodes.name: Regularity of $f$
nodes.statement:
Under (A)-(C), with $\alphab^\star(\x,\D)=\arg\min_{\alphab}  rac{1}{2}\|\x-\D\alphab\|_2^2 + \lambda\|\alphab\|_1$: (1) $\l$ is $C^1$ in $\D$ with $
abla_\D \l = -(\x-\D\alphab^\star)\alphab^{\star T}$; (2) $f$ is $C^1$ with $
abla f(\D) = \E_\x[
abla_\D \l(\x,\D)]$; (3) $
abla f$ is Lipschitz on $\C$.
assumptions: (B) strictly convex surrogates with lower-bounded Hessians

nodes.name: Convergence of $f(\D_t)$ and the surrogate function
nodes.statement: Under (A)-(C): (1) $\hatf_t(\D_t)$ converges almost surely; (2) $f(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t) \to 0$ a.s.; (3) $f(\D_t)$ converges almost surely.
assumptions: (B) strictly convex surrogates with lower-bounded Hessians

nodes.name: Convergence to a stationary point
nodes.statement: Under (A)-(C), the distance from $\D_t$ to the set of stationary points of the dictionary learning problem converges almost surely to $0$ as $t \to \infty$.
assumptions: (B) strictly convex surrogates with lower-bounded Hessians
conclusions: $\mathrm{dist}(\D_t, \mathcal{S}_\star) \to 0$ almost surely as $t \to \infty$, where $\mathcal{S}_\star$ is the stationary set

nodes.name: Projection onto the elastic-net constraint set
nodes.statement: For $\b \in \Real^m$, $\gamma \geq 0$, $\tau > 0$, Algorithm \ref{fig:proj_elastic} solves the elastic-net projection problem $\min_\u \frac{1}{2}\|\b-\u\|_2^2 \st \|\u\|_1+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\u\|_2^2 \leq \tau$.
conclusions: Algorithm \ref{fig:proj_elastic} returns the unique projection $\u^\star$ solving Eq.~(\ref{eq:proj})

nodes.name: Reduction lemma for fused-lasso signal approximation
nodes.statement: Let $\u^\star(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)$ solve Eq.~(\ref{eq:flsa}). Then (i) $\u^\star(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3) = \frac{1}{1+\gamma_3}\u^\star(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,0)$; (ii) $\u^\star(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,0)$ is obtained from $\u^\star(0,\gamma_2,0)$ by soft thresholding.
assumptions: $\u^\star(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3)$ solves the fused-lasso signal approximation Eq.~(\ref{eq:flsa})

nodes.name: Bonnans-Shapiro / Danskin differentiability of value function
nodes.statement:
If $f(\x,\u)$ and $
abla_\u f$ are continuous on $\Real^p 	imes \Real^q$, $C \subset \Real^p$ is compact and $f(\cdot,\u_0)$ has a unique minimizer $\x_0$, then $v(\u)=\min_{\x \in C} f(\x,\u)$ is differentiable at $\u_0$ with $
abla_\u v(\u_0) = 
abla_\u f(\x_0,\u_0)$.
conclusions: $v(\u)=\min_{\x \in C} f(\x,\u)$ is differentiable at $\u_0$ with $\nabla_\u v(\u_0) = \nabla_\u f(\x_0,\u_0)$

nodes.name: Quasi-martingale convergence (Fisk / Metivier)
nodes.statement: Let $u_t \geq 0$ and $\delta_t = \one[\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t]>0]$. If $\sum_t \E[\delta_t (u_{t+1}-u_t)] < \infty$, then $u_t$ is a quasi-martingale that converges a.s., and $\sum_t |\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t]| < \infty$ a.s.
assumptions: $u_t$ is a non-negative stochastic process adapted to $\FF_t$
conclusions: $u_t$ is a quasi-martingale and converges almost surely

nodes.name: Donsker-type empirical-process bound
nodes.statement: If $F=\{f_\theta:\theta \in \Theta\}$ is uniformly Lipschitz in $\theta$, $\Theta$ is bounded, and $\PPP f^2,\|f\|_\infty$ are uniformly bounded, then $\E\|\G_n\|_F = \O(1)$ where $\G_n f = \sqrt{n}(\PPP_n f - \PPP f)$.
assumptions: $\PPP f^2 < \delta^2$ and $\|f\|_\infty < M$ for all $f \in F$

nodes.name: Convergence of positive sums
nodes.statement: If $a_n,b_n \geq 0$, $\sum_n a_n = \infty$, $\sum_n a_n b_n < \infty$ and $|b_{n+1}-b_n| < K a_n$, then $b_n \to 0$.

nodes.name: Surrogate vs. empirical cost
nodes.statement: $\hatf_t$ is quadratic in $\D$ and upper-bounds the empirical cost $f_t(\D_t)$; the convergence analysis shows $\hatf_t(\D_t)$ and $f_t(\D_t)$ have the same almost-sure limit.

nodes.name: Warm restart for dictionary update
nodes.statement: Because $\hatf_t$ is close to $\hatf_{t-1}$ for large $t$, $\D_{t-1}$ is an effective warm restart for computing $\D_t$, and a single sweep of Algorithm \ref{fig:algoupdate} typically suffices in practice.

nodes.name: Two-epoch sliding-window for finite training sets
nodes.statement: Maintain auxiliary matrices $\A_t',\B_t'$ that get swapped into $\A_t,\B_t$ at the end of each epoch, ensuring no coefficient $\alphab_i$ older than two epochs contributes.

nodes.name: Slowing down first iterations via $t_0$
nodes.statement: Initialize $\A_0 = t_0 \I$ and $\B_0 = t_0 \D_0$ so the first dictionary updates stay close to $\D_0$, mimicking the $a/(t+b)$ trick in SGD.

nodes.name: Purging unused dictionary atoms
nodes.statement: Replace seldom-used columns by random training samples, optionally combined with a continuation strategy that gradually increases $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Online vs. batch dictionary learning on natural-image patches
nodes.statement: On data sets $A$ ($8\times 8$), $B$ ($12\times 12 \times 3$), and $C$ ($16\times 16$) of $10^6$ Pascal VOC'06 patches, the online algorithm consistently outperforms its batch counterpart (subsets of size $10^4,10^5,10^6$) on test-set objective vs. computation time.

nodes.name: Comparison with stochastic gradient descent
nodes.statement: On the same image-patch data sets, our online algorithm is competitive with carefully tuned mini-batch SGD with learning rate $a/(\eta t+b)$ but does not require this rate-tuning.

nodes.name: NMF and NNSC experiments
nodes.statement: On face data sets D ($n=2429$, MIT-CBCL), E ($n=2414$, Extended Yale B), and natural-patch set F ($n=10^5$), our method beats Lee \& Seung's NMF and Hoyer's NNSC in time-to-objective.

nodes.name: SPCA on faces and natural patches
nodes.statement: Qualitative comparison of PCA, NMF, dictionary learning, and SPCA on data sets D, E, F at sparsity levels $\tau \in \{70\%, 30\%, 10\%\}$ shows SPCA is the only method giving controllable sparsity in the learned matrices.

nodes.name: Genomic CCA on breast-cancer data
nodes.statement: Following Witten et al., on the breast-cancer data of Chin et al. ($q=2148$ gene expression, $p=16962$ CGH, $n=89$ samples), our method on Eq.~(\ref{eq:cancer}) achieves correlations across all 23 chromosomes comparable to penalized matrix decomposition (PMD).

nodes.name: Inpainting on a 12-Megapixel image
nodes.statement: A dictionary of $256$ atoms is learned in about 8 minutes on a 2.4GHz 8-core machine from $\sim 7\times 10^6$ undamaged $12\times 12$ color patches and used to remove text from a 12-Megapixel photograph via the inpainting technique of Mairal et al.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (Asymptotic variations of $\D_t$)
nodes.statement: Combine the second-order growth condition for the strictly convex surrogate $\hatf_t$ with the Lipschitz constant of $\hatf_t-\hatf_{t+1}$ to obtain $\|\D_{t+1}-\D_t\|_F \leq c_t/\kappa_1$ with $c_t = \O(1/t)$ a.s.

nodes.name: Second-order growth of $\hatf_t$
nodes.statement: By assumption (B), $\hatf_t$ is strictly convex with Hessian lower bounded by $\kappa_1$, hence $\hatf_t(\D_{t+1})-\hatf_t(\D_t) \geq \kappa_1 \|\D_{t+1}-\D_t\|_F^2$.

nodes.name: Telescoping bound using optimality of $\D_{t+1}$
nodes.statement: Decompose $\hatf_t(\D_{t+1})-\hatf_t(\D_t)$ via $\hatf_{t+1}$ and use $\hatf_{t+1}(\D_{t+1}) - \hatf_{t+1}(\D_t) \leq 0$ to bound it by $\hatf_t(\D_{t+1})-\hatf_{t+1}(\D_{t+1}) + \hatf_{t+1}(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t)$.

nodes.name: Lipschitzness of $\hatf_t-\hatf_{t+1}$
nodes.statement: Show $\hatf_t-\hatf_{t+1}$ is Lipschitz with constant $c_t=(1/t)(\|\B_{t+1}-\B_t\|_F + \sqrt{k}\|\A_{t+1}-\A_t\|_F)$, hence $\hatf_t(\D_{t+1})-\hatf_t(\D_t) \leq c_t \|\D_{t+1}-\D_t\|_F$.

nodes.name: Combine bounds and conclude
nodes.statement: From the two inequalities, $\|\D_{t+1}-\D_t\|_F \leq c_t/\kappa_1$. Assumptions (A) and (C) plus Eq.~(\ref{eq:closed}) give that $\alphab_i,\x_i$ are bounded a.s., hence $c_t = \O(1/t)$ a.s.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 (Regularity of $f$)
nodes.statement: Apply Bonnans-Shapiro / Danskin (Theorem A.1) to obtain differentiability of $\l$, exchange derivative and expectation under compactness, then prove $\alphab^\star(\x,\cdot)$ is uniformly Lipschitz to deduce Lipschitzness of $\nabla f$.

nodes.name: Boundedness and existence of $\alphab^\star$
nodes.statement: Assumption (A) gives boundedness of $\alphab^\star$ on a compact subset; assumption (C) gives uniqueness, so $\alphab^\star(\x,\D)$ is well defined.

nodes.name: Differentiability of $\l$ via Bonnans-Shapiro
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem A.1 (Bonnans-Shapiro / Danskin) to conclude $\l$ is $C^1$ in $\D$ with $\nabla_\D \l(\x,\D)=-(\x-\D\alphab^\star)\alphab^{\star T}$.

nodes.name: Differentiability of $f$ by exchange of derivative and expectation
nodes.statement: Since $K$ is compact and $\l$ is $C^1$, $f(\D)=\E_\x[\l(\x,\D)]$ is also $C^1$ with $\nabla f = \E_\x[\nabla_\D \l]$.

nodes.name: Local Lipschitzness of $\alphab^\star$
nodes.statement: Using $\tildel(\x,\D_\Lambda,\alphab_\Lambda)$ and the strict convexity of $\tildel(\x,\D_\Lambda,\cdot)$ (Hessian $\geq \kappa_2$), show $\|{\alphab^\star}'-\alphab^\star\|_2 \leq \frac{1}{\kappa_2}(e_1 \|\D-\D'\|_F + e_2 \|\x-\x'\|_2)$.

nodes.name: From local to uniform Lipschitz on the compact set
nodes.statement: Since $K\times \C$ is compact, the local Lipschitz property extends uniformly, so $\nabla f$ is Lipschitz on $\C$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2 (Convergence of surrogate)
nodes.statement: Show $u_t = \hatf_t(\D_t) \geq 0$ is a quasi-martingale via Donsker-type bound on $\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t]^+$, apply Theorem A.2 (Fisk) to get a.s. convergence, then use Lemma 1 and Lemma A.3 to deduce $f_t(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t)\to 0$ and hence $f(\D_t)$ converges a.s.

nodes.name: Define $u_t = \hatf_t(\D_t)$ and compute its variation
nodes.statement: Let $u_t = \hatf_t(\D_t) \geq 0$ and expand $u_{t+1}-u_t$ using $\hatf_{t+1}(\D_t)=\frac{1}{t+1}\l(\x_{t+1},\D_t) + \frac{t}{t+1}\hatf_t(\D_t)$.

nodes.name: Conditional bound on $\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t]$
nodes.statement: Use $\hatf_{t+1}(\D_{t+1}) - \hatf_{t+1}(\D_t)\leq 0$ and $f_t(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t)\leq 0$ to bound $\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t] \leq \|f-f_t\|_\infty/(t+1)$.

nodes.name: Apply Donsker-type Lemma A.3
nodes.statement: Lemma A.3 (Donsker corollary) yields $\E[\sqrt{t}\|f-f_t\|_\infty]=O(1)$, so $\E[\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t]^+] \leq \kappa/t^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Apply quasi-martingale theorem
nodes.statement: Theorem A.2 (Fisk quasi-martingale convergence) gives $u_t = \hatf_t(\D_t)$ converges a.s. and $\sum_t |\E[u_{t+1}-u_t|\FF_t]| < \infty$ a.s.

nodes.name: Deduce $f_t(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t)\to 0$ via Lemma A.4
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 1 and the boundedness/Lipschitzness of $f_t,\hatf_t$ together with Lemma A.4 (positive sum convergence) to conclude $f_t(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t)\to 0$ a.s.

nodes.name: Glivenko-Cantelli closes the proof
nodes.statement: Glivenko-Cantelli ($\|f_t-f\|_\infty \to 0$ a.s.) plus the previous step yield $f(\D_t)-\hatf_t(\D_t)\to 0$ a.s. and $f(\D_t)$ converges a.s.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3 (Stationarity)
nodes.statement: Extract a converging subsequence of $(\A_t,\B_t)$, pass to the limit in $\hatf_t \geq f_t$, use first-order Taylor expansion to obtain $\nabla \hatf_\infty(\D_\infty) = \nabla f(\D_\infty)$, then conclude that the normal-cone optimality condition for $f$ is satisfied at $\D_\infty$ asymptotically.

nodes.name: Compactness and subsequential limits
nodes.statement: $(\A_t,\B_t)$ live in a compact set, so extract converging subsequences with limits $\A_\infty,\B_\infty$, inducing $\D_t \to \D_\infty \in \C$.

nodes.name: Pass surrogate inequality to the limit
nodes.statement: From $\hatf_t(\D_t+\U) \geq f_t(\D_t+\U)$, take $t \to \infty$ to get $\hatf_\infty(\D_\infty+\U) \geq f(\D_\infty+\U)$.

nodes.name: First-order Taylor expansion
nodes.statement:
Use Lipschitzness of $
abla f$ and $\hatf_\infty(\D_\infty)=f(\D_\infty)$ a.s. to deduce $
abla \hatf_\infty(\D_\infty) = 
abla f(\D_\infty)$.

nodes.name: Normal-cone optimality and conclusion
nodes.statement:
Since $-
abla \hatf_\infty(\D_\infty)$ lies in the normal cone of $\C$ at $\D_\infty$ and $
abla \hatf_\infty=
abla f$ at the limit, the same holds for $f$, so first-order optimality is verified asymptotically a.s.

nodes.name: Proof that Algorithm 3 solves the elastic-net projection
nodes.statement: Form the Lagrangian, derive the closed-form $\u^\star(\lambda)$, use Slater's condition + complementary slackness to characterize the optimal multiplier $\lambda^\star$ via the support set $S(\lambda^\star)$, then show that lines 4-14 of Algorithm \ref{fig:proj_elastic} identify $S(\lambda^\star)$ in expected linear time.

nodes.name: Set up the Lagrangian and dual
nodes.statement: Define $\L(\u,\lambda) = \frac{1}{2}\|\b-\u\|_2^2 + \lambda(\|\u\|_1 + \frac{\gamma}{2}\|\u\|_2^2 - \tau)$ and reduce to the dual $\max_{\lambda \geq 0} \L(\u^\star(\lambda),\lambda)$ since Slater's condition holds.

nodes.name: Closed-form primal solution given $\lambda$
nodes.statement: $\u^\star(\lambda)[j] = \frac{\sign(\b[j])(|\b[j]|-\lambda)^+}{1+\lambda\gamma}$, an elastic-net soft-thresholding map.

nodes.name: Complementary slackness and monotonicity
nodes.statement: Strict monotonicity of $\lambda \mapsto \|\u^\star(\lambda)\|_1+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\u^\star(\lambda)\|_2^2$ makes $\|\u^\star(\lambda^\star)\|_1+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\u^\star(\lambda^\star)\|_2^2 = \tau$ a necessary and sufficient optimality condition.

nodes.name: Reformulate as support-set selection
nodes.statement: Show optimality reduces to $\frac{1}{(1+\lambda\gamma)^2}\sum_{j \in S(\lambda)}(|\b[j]|+\frac{\gamma}{2}|\b[j]|^2 - \lambda(1+\frac{\gamma\lambda}{2})) = \tau$, with $S(\lambda)=\{j:|\b[j]|\geq \lambda\}$.

nodes.name: Algorithm correctness via Duchi-style partition
nodes.statement: Lines 4-14 of Algorithm \ref{fig:proj_elastic} are a Duchi-type randomized partition that finds $S(\lambda^\star)$ in expected $\O(m)$, after which lines 15-18 give $\lambda^\star$ in closed form. Setting $\gamma=0$ recovers the algorithm of Duchi et al.

nodes.name: Initialize sufficient statistics
nodes.statement: $\A_0 \in \Real^{k \times k} \leftarrow 0$; $\B_0 \in \Real^{m \times k} \leftarrow 0$.

nodes.name: Main online loop over $t = 1,\ldots,T$
nodes.statement: For $t=1$ to $T$: draw $\x_t \sim p(\x)$, perform sparse coding to get $\alphab_t$, accumulate $\A_t,\B_t$, then update the dictionary by calling Algorithm \ref{fig:algoupdate} with $\D_{t-1}$ as warm restart.

nodes.name: Sparse coding via LARS
nodes.statement: $\alphab_t \defin \arg\min_{\alphab \in \Real^k} \frac{1}{2}\|\x_t - \D_{t-1}\alphab\|_2^2 + \lambda\|\alphab\|_1$, computed with LARS-Lasso.

nodes.name: Update sufficient statistics
nodes.statement: $\A_t \leftarrow \A_{t-1} + \alphab_t \alphab_t^T$; $\B_t \leftarrow \B_{t-1} + \x_t \alphab_t^T$.

nodes.name: Dictionary update
nodes.statement: $\D_t \defin \arg\min_{\D \in \C} \frac{1}{t}\big(\frac{1}{2}\trace(\D^T\D\A_t) - \trace(\D^T\B_t)\big)$ via Algorithm \ref{fig:algoupdate}.

nodes.name: Return learned dictionary
nodes.statement: Return $\D_T$.

nodes.name: Outer convergence loop over columns
nodes.statement: Repeat until convergence: for $j=1,\ldots,k$, update column $\d_j$ via the closed-form per-column update (Eq.~\ref{eq:updated}).

nodes.name: Per-column closed-form update
nodes.statement: $\u_j \leftarrow \frac{1}{\A[j,j]}(\b_j - \D \a_j) + \d_j$; $\d_j \leftarrow \frac{1}{\max(\|\u_j\|_2, 1)}\u_j$.

nodes.name: Return updated dictionary
nodes.statement: Return $\D$.

nodes.name: Feasibility test
nodes.statement: If $\|\b\|_1 + \frac{\gamma}{2}\|\b\|_2^2 \leq \tau$, return $\u \leftarrow \b$; else proceed with the active-set search.

nodes.name: Initialize partition variables
nodes.statement: $U \leftarrow \{1,\ldots,m\}$; $s \leftarrow 0$; $\rho \leftarrow 0$.

nodes.name: Randomized partition loop
nodes.statement: While $U \neq \emptyset$: pick a random pivot $k \in U$, partition $U$ into $G=\{j:|\b[j]| \geq |\b[k]|\}$ and $L=\{j:|\b[j]|<|\b[k]|\}$, accumulate $\Delta\rho=|G|, \Delta s=\sum_{j\in G}(|\b[j]|+\frac{\gamma}{2}|\b[j]|^2)$, and recurse on $L$ or $G\setminus\{k\}$ depending on whether $s+\Delta s - (\rho+\Delta\rho)(1+\frac{\gamma}{2}|\b[k]|)|\b[k]| < \tau(1+\gamma|\b[k]|)^2$.

nodes.name: Compute $\lambda^\star$ in closed form
nodes.statement: Set $a=\gamma^2 \tau + \frac{\gamma}{2}\rho$, $b=2\gamma\tau+\rho$, $c=\tau-s$ and $\lambda \leftarrow \frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$.

nodes.name: Apply elastic-net soft thresholding and return
nodes.statement: For each $j$, $\u[j] \leftarrow \frac{\sign(\b[j])(|\b[j]|-\lambda)^+}{1+\lambda\gamma}$; return $\u$.
